subject: project:gdl
value: `gdlmem validate` DID NOT COMPLETE BECAUSE IT WAS QUADRATIC, NOT BECAUSE THE CORPUS IS BIG, AND IT NOW RUNS IN UNDER A SECOND. AGENTS.md discipline 13 told every lane to skip it ('does not complete at current corpus size -- never block on it'), which left the only whole-corpus schema check unusable and made `build` the de-facto integrity gate. MEASURED BASELINE, by cProfile on the unmodified code: 1526.81 s for 1568 records, and the profile names the mechanism outright -- 1568 calls to `_probe_record_references` produced 1547 calls to `ensure_database` and 1552 calls to `source_fingerprint`, costing 1489 s of the 1526 s, via 10,618,930 `nt._getfinalpathname` calls (653 s) and 8,285,013 `nt.stat` calls (389 s). `ensure_database` recomputes the fingerprint by stat-ing every record file, both symbol tables, the PDB dump and every tools/gdl source, roughly 1,600 stats, and it was being called ONCE PER RECORD. FIX: hoist the database out of the loop (one connection, one ensure) and memoise per-record results by content hash. Schema validation is a pure function of the record bytes so its cache key is the content hash alone; reference resolution depends on the whole graph so its key additionally carries the database's source_fingerprint, which changes whenever any record does -- a corpus that changed at all therefore revalidates every reference. MEASURED AFTER: 0.453 s cold, 0.250 s warm, 1568/1568 schema and reference checks served from cache on the warm run. A ~3,400x reduction, from never-completes to a routine gate. IMMEDIATE DIVIDEND, and the reason an unusable check is expensive rather than merely absent: the first completing run surfaced 61 dangling citations across the ACCEPTED corpus that no lane could previously see. They are classified as DEBT rather than as a validation failure, because most are the documented `prune-attempts` workflow's own output -- it DELETES records ejected past the per-function cap, stranding every `supersedes` that pointed at one -- and failing the corpus on them would make the gate refuse the workflow that documents it. New proposals stay STRICT: a dangling citation at staging is still refused.
